title: Review of c45's Marangoni swim screen on fresh seeds 72 and 73: mar 60 lengthens per-cycle swims on seed 73 (median D 1.30 -> 2.04, p=0.016) but not on seed 72 (1.47 -> 1.36, p=0.42); path speed rises on both, divisions are kept
summary: Re-ran c34's Marangoni world with the screen's command (CARGO 0, 128^2, T=1000, 200 frames) at base (mar 40) and mar 60 on seeds 72 and 73, built per-track tables with c00's extract.py and summarised with the screen's stats.py (stats.txt) and a Mann-Whitney test (mw.txt). Seed 72: median per-cycle D of dividing rods 1.36 (mar 60) vs 1.47 (base), share D >= 2.5 0.06 vs 0.07, persistent splits 30 vs 27. Seed 73: 2.04 vs 1.30, share 0.20 vs 0.00, splits 23 vs 27. Pooled: 1.42 vs 1.34, one-sided p=0.08. Path speed of dividing rods rises on both seeds (0.293 vs 0.178; 0.313 vs 0.243), but on seed 72 the mar 60 rods swim less straight (0.75 vs 0.85), so the extra speed does not become net distance.

observations.finding: stats.txt: seed 73 reproduces the shift (median D 2.04 vs 1.30, share >= 2.5 0.20 vs 0, p=0.016) and keeps 85% of divisions; seed 72 does not (1.36 vs 1.47, p=0.42) although path speed rises 0.178 -> 0.293; runs/mar60/seed72/sheet.png shows the same curved, dividing rods as base

seeds_run.result: fail (no distance shift; speed up, straightness down)

controls_run.finding: same-seed base runs (mar 40) on seeds 72 and 73

verdicts.limitation: Two fresh seeds with 10-18 dividing rods each, so per-seed tests have little power; together with the screen's seeds 70 and 71 the effect is 3 of 4 seeds. The robust part is that mar 60 speeds the rods up without cutting divisions; whether that becomes longer per-cycle displacement depends on how straight the rods swim. mar 80 and the other screened settings were not rerun.
